subject: "Not encrypted" text messages (RCS and SMS)
query: what does text message not encrypted mean
title: What does text message not encrypted mean? Your chat isn't locked
answer: It means that conversation isn't end-to-end encrypted, so the message travels in a form your carrier or anyone intercepting it could read, the way ordinary SMS always has. Your phone isn't broken or hacked; it's simply telling you that this chat isn't getting the lock-protected version of texting.
body:
Phones now send texts in three main ways. iMessage (iPhone to iPhone) and Google Messages chats between Android phones are end-to-end encrypted, so only the sender and recipient can read them. Plain SMS and MMS are not encrypted at all. RCS, the newer standard that adds typing indicators and high-quality photos, can go either way: an RCS chat is encrypted only when both phones, their apps and the carriers all support encrypted RCS. When any piece is missing, the app labels the chat or message as not encrypted. A typical case: "My texts to my mom say not encrypted since she switched phones."

Apple added end-to-end encrypted RCS in iOS 26.5, which began testing in May 2026. It works in one-on-one chats between an iPhone and an Android phone using an up-to-date app that supports the industry (GSMA) standard, on a supported carrier. Group chats, including any group with an Android member, are not covered, and neither are details like who you texted and when. On iPhone, a lock and "Encrypted" note appears in protected chats, and the conversation's info screen shows whether RCS is encrypted. A chat can also quietly drop to an unencrypted mode, for example when someone joins a group or service is spotty and the message falls back to SMS.

You may also see an offer to "send without encryption." That generally means the protected route isn't available right now, and the app is asking whether to deliver the message anyway over an unencrypted one. For everyday messages that's usually fine; for passwords, bank details or anything sensitive, use a chat that shows the lock or say it in person. Searches for "what does send without encryption mean" and "what does text message not encrypted mean" have climbed this month as more people notice the new labels.

What you can do: update your phone and messaging app, make sure RCS is turned on (on iPhone, Settings > Apps > Messages), and ask the other person to do the same. If it still says not encrypted, the cause is often their carrier or an older phone, and there's nothing wrong on your side.
in_the_news: Encrypted texting between iPhones and Android phones arrived in 2026, so more people are now seeing labels that tell them which chats are, and aren't, protected.

faq.q: Does not encrypted mean my phone was hacked?
faq.a: No. It only means that chat doesn't use end-to-end encryption, usually because one phone, app or carrier doesn't support it.

faq.q: What does send without encryption mean?
faq.a: The protected route isn't available, and the app is asking whether to send the message over an unencrypted one, like a regular text.

faq.q: Are iPhone to Android texts encrypted?
faq.a: They can be, in one-on-one RCS chats on iOS 26.5 or later with a supported app and carrier. Group chats and plain SMS are not.

faq.q: How do I make my texts encrypted?
faq.a: Update your phone and messaging app, turn on RCS, and use iMessage, Google Messages or another end-to-end encrypted app. Both people need support for it.
